37	---
38	title: "Match Audio"
39	description: "Give several clips the loudness and speech tone of one of them, so takes from different microphones or rooms sit together, in one undo step."
40	---
41	
42	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
43	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
44	
45	Match Audio makes selected clips sound like one of them, the reference. It sets each other clip's loudness and speech tone in one undo step, which helps when two takes came from different microphones or rooms.
46	
47	<AtAGlance
48	  menu="Clip ▸ Match Audio…"
49	  tools="match_audio"
50	  needs="Nothing. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
51	/>
52	
53	## Match clips to a reference
54	
55	<Steps>
56	
57	1. Select the clips, including the one that already sounds right. You need at least two clips that could play sound. A nest clip or a clip with no sound doesn't count, and with fewer than two the menu item is dimmed.
58	
59	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Match Audio…**.
60	
61	3. In **Match to:**, choose the reference.
62	
63	4. Leave **Loudness** and **EQ** ticked, or untick the one you don't want. **Match** is greyed out with both off.
64	
65	5. Choose **Match**.
66	
67	</Steps>
68	
69	The Measuring Sound sheet stays up while each clip is measured as it plays, which takes a moment on a long clip. It counts "Clip 1 of 3…" as it goes. Nothing changes until every clip is measured, and **Cancel** leaves everything as it is.
70	
71	When it finishes, the change is one undo step called "Match Audio". The results are ordinary settings in the [Volume](/audio/volume/), [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) and [EQ](/audio/eq/) sections, so you can adjust them afterwards.
72	
73	The sheet opens with both boxes ticked and the first clip chosen every time. It doesn't remember your last choice.
74	
75	## Choose the reference
76	
77	**Match to:** lists the clips in timeline order, by start time and then by track, and the first is chosen. Each row reads `name — track — m:ss (clip id)`, for example `Interview — Track 1 — 0:42 (clip 12)`, so you can tell two clips with the same name apart.
78	
79	The reference itself isn't changed. Frame Job measures it once as it sounds in the timeline: through its own settings, its limiter and its volume, but without its fades, ducking or Mute. Its loudness at that point is the target for the other clips.
80	
81	## What Loudness sets
82	
83	**Loudness** runs [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode on each other clip, with the reference's loudness as the target. It sets the clip's volume, measured through the clip's settings as they'll be after the match. When the clip's peaks would pass −1 dBTP at that loudness, it also sets the clip's limiter at that ceiling.
84	
85	A clip so quiet that it needs more than the volume's ceiling of 32× stops there and ends up quieter than the reference.
86	
87	Loudness doesn't need speech, so you can use it on music by unticking **EQ**.
88	
89	## What EQ sets
90	
91	**EQ** gives each other clip the tone of the reference's voice. Frame Job compares the average spectrum of each clip's speech with the reference's, in 23 third-octave bands from 79 Hz to 12.7 kHz. Only speech counts: the spans saved for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) when there are any, otherwise what speech detection found in the file. A clip needs about a second of speech.
92	
93	Each clip is measured with its EQ's shelves and bands off. The difference, less the overall level, is then fitted with the EQ's low shelf, three bands and high shelf:
94	
95	- Each gain stays within ±12 dB.
96	- Each band's Q stays between 0.5 and 4.
97	- A band is only used where the difference is at least 0.5 dB.
98	
99	Those five parts replace the clip's own. Its high-pass, low-pass and [hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/) stay as they were, and **Bypass** is turned off.
100	
101	## What stays the same
102	
103	Match Audio writes only volume, limiter and EQ. Every other section, the fades, ducking, pan and Mute are left alone.
104	
105	Choosing **Match** again with the same choice changes nothing. Frame Job beeps and adds no undo step.
106	
107	## When a clip can't be matched
108	
109	A clip that can't be matched is skipped, and the others are still matched. No message names a skipped clip, so if one sounds unchanged, check it against the list below.
110	
111	If the reference can't be used, or nothing can be matched, Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and puts the reason at the foot of the inspector. A reference's reason starts "The reference, clip 12,". When every clip fails, it starts "Nothing could be matched." and gives each clip's reason.
112	
113	| The reason says | What it means | What to do |
114	| --- | --- | --- |
115	| "is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured yet" | Frame Job hasn't finished with the file, which often happens straight after an import. | Try again in a moment. |
116	| "is still being analysed — its speech has not been detected yet" | The same, for speech. This only applies with **EQ** on. | Try again in a moment, or untick **EQ**. |
117	| "plays no sound in this timeline" | Nothing from this clip reaches the mix. | Choose another clip. |
118	| "plays for under 0.4 s" | The clip is too short to have a loudness. | Choose a longer clip, or trim this one longer. |
119	| "is under −70 LUFS" | There's no sound to match. | Choose another clip. |
120	| "has under 1 s of speech" | The part that plays has too little speech to measure a tone. | Untick **EQ**, or choose a clip with more speech. |
121	| "has under 12 third-octave bands within 50 dB of its loudest" | The reference's sound is too narrow to match a tone to. | Choose another reference, or untick **EQ**. |
122	| "shares under 12 third-octave bands with the reference" | This clip and the reference have too little of the spectrum in common. | Match this clip again with **EQ** unticked. |
123	
124	If the project changes while the clips are being measured, nothing is applied. Frame Job beeps, and the foot of the inspector says "the project changed while its sound was being measured, so nothing changed. Choose Match Audio again."
125	
126	## Good to know
127	
128	- Match Audio matches the average tone of speech. It doesn't match the room, reverb, noise or dynamics. For those, see [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/), [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/).
129	- You match to a clip, not to a track or a whole mix.
130	- Like Normalize, it writes each clip's own settings even with an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected.
131	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, it works on the clips inside the nest.
132	
133	## With an agent
134	
135	`match_audio` takes the reference and the clips directly, with no sheet. Unlike the menu, it answers with what happened to each clip, including each skipped clip and why. A nest can't be matched or used as the reference, and the call fails if Loudness and EQ are both off. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).
136	
137	## Related
138	
139	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)
140	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
141	- [EQ](/audio/eq/)
142	- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
143	=== voice-isolation
144	---
145	title: "Voice Isolation"
146	description: "Keep the voice in a clip and remove background noise and room echo, using Apple's voice model on your Mac."
147	---
148	
149	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
150	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
151	
152	Voice Isolation keeps the voice in a clip and removes what's around it: background noise and the echo of the room. It uses Apple's on-device voice model, so nothing leaves your Mac.
153	
154	<AtAGlance
155	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Isolation"
156	  tools="set_audio"
157	  needs="Nothing. The voice model runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
158	/>
159	
160	## Isolate a voice
161	
162	<Steps>
163	
164	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Voice Isolation** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
165	
166	2. Tick **Isolate voice**. The Amount goes to 80 % and **Status** reads "Rendering…".
167	
168	3. Keep working. The clip plays without isolation until **Status** reads "Ready", then the editor switches over by itself.
169	
170	4. Listen, and change **Amount** if you need to.
171	
172	</Steps>
173	
174	Isolation also reduces room echo, so there's no separate control for reverb.
175	
176	## The controls
177	
178	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
179	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
180	| **Isolate voice** | Turns isolation on at 80 %, or off. | On or off | Off |
181	| **Amount** | How much of the isolated voice replaces the clip's own sound. Quick values: 50, 80 and 100 %. | 0 to 100 % | 0 % (off) |
182	| **Status** | What the isolated voice is doing. See [What Status says](#what-status-says). | | Off |
183	
184	Setting **Amount** above 0 also turns isolation on, and 0 turns it off. **Reset** in the section's header does the same as unticking the box.
185	
186	## Choose an amount
187	
188	Amount blends the isolated voice with the clip's own sound.
189	
190	- **At 80 %**, the pauses between words drop by about 14 dB and keep a little of the room, so the voice doesn't sit in dead silence. This is what the box turns on.
191	- **At 100 %**, the pauses are silent.
192	- **Below that**, more of the original sound comes through.
193	
194	Changing Amount takes effect at once. It doesn't need the isolated voice to be worked out again.
195	
196	## While it renders
197	
198	The isolated voice is worked out once for each clip, in the background, when you turn it on. Until it's ready the clip plays without it, and the editor switches over by itself.
199	
200	Trimming or slipping the clip works it out again, because the clip then plays a different part of its file.
201	
202	An export waits for every isolated clip to be ready, and its sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name while it does, so a file is never written without isolation. If a clip's isolated voice can't be made, the export stops with "Clip 12's isolated voice could not be rendered:" and the reason.
203	
204	## What Status says
205	
206	| Status | What it means |
207	| --- | --- |
208	| Off | Isolation is off for this clip. |
209	| Rendering… | The isolated voice is being worked out. The clip plays without it for now. |
210	| Ready | The clip plays with isolation. |
211	| Plays without it at this speed | The clip has a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame. See below. |
212	| Waits for the reversed copy | The clip is reversed, and its reversed copy isn't ready yet. |
213	| Not rendered: and a reason | It failed, for example "Not rendered: its media cannot be found". |
214	| — | Several clips are selected. |
215	
216	## Speed, ramps and freeze frames
217	
218	Isolation plays only at normal speed. A clip with a [speed change](/speed/change-speed/), a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) or a [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) plays without it, and **Status** says so.
219	
220	A [reversed](/speed/reverse/) clip is isolated once its reversed copy is ready.
221	
222	## Good to know
223	
224	- Isolation comes first in the clip's sound, before the channel choice, the EQ, noise reduction and the compressor. You can use it with [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/), which then works on the isolated sound. A [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) is made from the isolated voice too. See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
225	- Two clips cut from one take are isolated separately, so the sound at the join may differ slightly.
226	- Isolation does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip, and its **Status** reads "Off". Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
227	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, **Isolate voice** and **Amount** write the action's end, and the Amount glides across the action, from 0 when the clip's own Amount is 0. The isolated voice is still made for a clip whose own isolation is off.
228	
229	## With an agent
230	
231	`set_audio` sets the amount from 0 to 1. An agent can't read **Status**, because the render's state isn't in `get_project`, but an export still waits for it. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
232	
233	## Related
234	
235	- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
236	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
237	- [Voice effects](/audio/voice-effects/)
238	- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)
239	=== noise-reduction
240	---
241	title: "Noise Reduction"
242	description: "Turn down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fans, under speech as well as between words, with no noise sample needed."
243	---
244	
245	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
246	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
247	
248	Noise Reduction turns down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fan noise. It works out the noise level from the clip itself, so you don't need to give it a sample of the noise or a stretch of silence.
249	
250	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Noise Reduction" tools="set_audio" />
251	
252	## Remove noise
253	
254	<Steps>
255	
256	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Noise Reduction** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
257	
258	2. Raise **Remove noise** while you listen, until the noise is low enough and the voice still sounds natural.
259	
260	</Steps>
261	
262	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
263	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
264	| **Remove noise** | How much steady background noise to remove. Quick values: 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %. | 0 to 100 % | 0 % (off) |
265	| **Depth** | Read-only. See [The Depth read-out](#the-depth-read-out). | | off |
266	
267	**Reset** in the section's header sets **Remove noise** back to 0.
268	
269	## The Depth read-out
270	
271	**Depth** tells you the most any part of the sound can be turned down at this setting. It follows **Remove noise**:
272	
273	| Remove noise | Depth reads |
274	| --- | --- |
275	| 0 % | off |
276	| 25 % | 2 dB at most |
277	| 50 % | 6 dB at most |
278	| 75 % | 12 dB at most |
279	| 100 % | floor removed |
280	
281	Noise Reduction never removes more than the noise level it found, so a higher setting isn't a stronger cut across the whole sound.
282	
283	## What it can't do
284	
285	Noise Reduction isn't a gate. It works under speech as well as between words, and it doesn't silence the gaps. To turn the pauses down, use the [Gate](/audio/gate/).
286	
287	It can't remove a sound that isn't steady, such as a door slam or a cough. A long held note may eventually be treated as noise.
288	
289	To reduce the echo of a room, use [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/). The two work together: Noise Reduction then works on the isolated sound.
290	
291	## Good to know
292	
293	- It runs after the EQ and [hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/), and before the [Gate](/audio/gate/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
294	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, **Remove noise** writes the action's end and the amount glides across the action.
295	- Noise Reduction set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
296	
297	## Related
298	
299	- [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
300	- [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/)
301	- [Gate](/audio/gate/)
302	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
303	- [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/)
304	=== hum-removal
305	---
306	title: "Hum removal"
307	description: "Notch out mains hum at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, and leave the voice between them alone."
308	---
309	
310	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
311	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
312	
313	Hum removal cuts the low electrical hum that mains power can leave on a recording. It places a narrow notch at the mains frequency and at each of its multiples, and leaves the sound between the notches alone.
314	
315	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Hum" tools="set_audio" />
316	
317	## Remove hum
318	
319	<Steps>
320	
321	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Hum** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
322	
323	2. Tick **Remove hum**. It starts at 60 Hz, 30 dB deep, with 4 harmonics.
324	
325	3. Set **Mains** to the frequency where the recording was made.
326	
327	4. If you can still hear the hum, raise **Depth** or **Harmonics**.
328	
329	</Steps>
330	
331	The other controls are dimmed until **Remove hum** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns hum removal off.
332	
333	## The controls
334	
335	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
336	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
337	| **Remove hum** | Turns hum removal on. | On or off | Off |
338	| **Mains** | The mains frequency where the recording was made. | 50 Hz or 60 Hz | 60 Hz |
339	| **Depth** | How far each notch turns the hum down. Quick values: 12, 24, 30 and 48 dB. | 6 to 60 dB | 30 dB |
340	| **Harmonics** | How many notches: the mains frequency and its multiples. Quick values: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 1 to 8 | 4 |
341	
342	At 60 Hz with 4 harmonics, the notches sit at 60, 120, 180 and 240 Hz.
343	
344	Each notch is about a tenth of the mains frequency wide, whatever its depth, so a notch at 60 Hz is about 6 Hz wide.
345	
346	## Good to know
347	
348	- Hum removal runs after the [EQ](/audio/eq/). Its notches appear in the EQ section's drawn curve, but the EQ's **Bypass** doesn't turn them off.
349	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls write the action's end. **Depth** glides across the action. **Mains**, **Harmonics** and turning hum removal on or off change at the action's end, with no glide.
350	- Hum removal set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
351	
352	## Related
353	
354	- [EQ](/audio/eq/)
355	- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
356	- [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/)
357	- [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/)
358	=== gate
359	---
360	title: "Gate"
361	description: "Turn a clip down in the pauses between phrases, so room noise and breaths get quieter while the speech stays as it is."
362	---
363	
364	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
365	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
366	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
367	
368	The gate turns a clip down in its pauses. When the sound falls below the threshold it's pushed further down, so room noise and breaths between phrases get quieter while the speech itself is untouched.
369	
370	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Gate" tools="set_audio" />
371	
372	<Shot
373	  name="09c-clip-sound-dynamics.inspector"
374	  alt="The Gate section of the Sound tab with Gate pauses ticked: Threshold −10 dB, Ratio 4.0:1, Range 20 dB, Attack 1 ms, Hold 50 ms, Release 100 ms, Status reading Opens above −31.8 dBFS, and Loudness −21.8 LUFS."
375	/>
376	
377	## Gate the pauses
378	
379	<Steps>
380	
381	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Gate** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
382	
383	2. Tick **Gate pauses**. It starts at the [defaults](#the-controls), which work from the clip's own loudness.
384	
385	3. Play the clip. If the ends of words are being cut, raise **Hold** or lower **Threshold**.
386	
387	4. If the pauses aren't quiet enough, raise **Range**. If they sound too empty, lower it.
388	
389	</Steps>
390	
391	The other controls are dimmed until **Gate pauses** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the gate off.
392	
393	## The controls
394	
395	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick values |
396	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
397	| **Threshold** | How far under the clip's loudness the gate opens. | −40 to 0 dB | −10 dB | −20, −15, −10, −6 |
398	| **Ratio** | How strongly sound under the threshold is turned down. At 4:1, each dB under the threshold becomes 3 dB further down. | 1:1 to 20:1 | 4:1 | 2, 4, 10, 20 |
399	| **Range** | The most the gate ever takes away. | 1 to 80 dB | 20 dB | 10, 20, 40, 80 |
400	| **Attack** | How quickly it opens when the sound rises. | 0 to 100 ms | 1 ms | 1, 5, 10 |
401	| **Hold** | How long it stays open after the sound falls, so the ends of words aren't clipped. | 0 to 500 ms | 50 ms | 0, 50, 100, 200 |
402	| **Release** | How quickly it closes after the hold. | 1 to 2,000 ms | 100 ms | 50, 100, 250, 500 |
403	
404	## The threshold follows the clip
405	
406	**Threshold** is set in dB under the clip's own loudness, not at a fixed level, so the same setting works on a quiet recording and a loud one. A trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves the loudness, and the threshold moves with it.
407	
408	That loudness is the Loudness figure in the [Volume](/audio/volume/) section. It's measured before noise reduction, the compressor, the volume, the fades and ducking, so moving the Volume slider doesn't change where the gate opens.
409	
410	## Read Status and Loudness
411	
412	Two read-outs at the foot of the section show what the threshold means for this clip. With several clips selected, **Loudness** reads "—". **Status** does too, unless the gate is off on the first of them, when it reads "off".
413	
414	**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−21.8 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.
415	
416	**Status** says where the gate opens, or why it isn't working:
417	
418	| Status | What it means |
419	| --- | --- |
420	| off | **Gate pauses** isn't ticked. |
421	| Opens above −31.8 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. Here, −21.8 LUFS with a −10 dB threshold. |
422	| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. See below. |
423	| Not gating: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
424	| Not gating: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
425	| Not gating: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |
426	
427	## Before the clip's loudness is measured
428	
429	The gate, the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) all depend on the clip's measured loudness. Until it lands, the clip plays without them, and the preview picks them up by itself.
430	
431	An export waits until every gated, levelled or de-essed clip has been measured. After five minutes without a measurement it stops, saying that the clip's loudness or speech hasn't been measured yet, and to wait for the Status rows to show the clip's loudness and export again.
432	
433	A clip that can't be measured, because it's under 0.4 s or too quiet, plays and exports without them, and the export doesn't wait for it.
434	
435	## Good to know
436	
437	- The gate runs after [noise reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and before the leveller, the de-esser and the [compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
438	- The gate doesn't look ahead, so a loud start after a long pause can lose its first moment while the gate opens. At the default **Attack**, that's about a millisecond.
439	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls write the action's end. The numbers glide across the action, and turning the gate on or off changes at the action's end.
440	- The gate does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
441	
442	## Related
443	
444	- [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
445	- [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/)
446	- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
447	- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
448	- [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/)
449	=== de-esser
450	---
451	title: "De-esser"
452	description: "Tame the hard s, sh and t sounds a close microphone exaggerates, turning down only the top of the voice while they last."
453	---
454	
455	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
456	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
457	
458	The de-esser tames sibilance, the hard "s", "sh" and "t" sounds a close microphone exaggerates. It listens to the sound above its frequency and turns only that band down while it's over the threshold, so the rest of the voice keeps its level.
459	
460	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ De-esser" tools="set_audio" />
461	
462	## Reduce sibilance
463	
464	<Steps>
465	
466	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **De-esser** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
467	
468	2. Tick **Reduce sibilance**. It starts at 6,000 Hz, a threshold of 0 dB and a range of 6 dB.
469	
470	3. Play a part with hard "s" sounds. If they're still sharp, lower **Threshold** or raise **Range**.
471	
472	4. If the voice sounds dull or lisped, raise **Threshold** or lower **Range**. Move **Frequency** to where the sibilance sits in this voice.
473	
474	</Steps>
475	
476	The other controls are dimmed until **Reduce sibilance** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the de-esser off.
477	
478	## The controls
479	
480	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick values |
481	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
482	| **Frequency** | Where the sibilant band starts. | 2,000 to 12,000 Hz | 6,000 Hz | 4,000, 5,000, 6,000, 8,000 |
483	| **Threshold** | How loud the band must get, relative to the clip's loudness, before it's turned down. | −30 to +20 dB | 0 dB | −6, −3, 0, 3 |
484	| **Range** | The most the band is turned down. | 1 to 24 dB | 6 dB | 3, 6, 10 |
485	
486	The de-esser never makes any frequency louder. Right at **Frequency** it takes less than half the range, about 2.5 dB of the default 6 dB, and about 5.5 dB an octave above.
487	
488	It reacts in 1 ms and lets go over 60 ms. You can't change those times.
489	
490	## Read Status and Loudness
491	
492	**Threshold** follows the clip's own loudness, the way the [Gate's](/audio/gate/#the-threshold-follows-the-clip) does, so a trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves it. Two read-outs show what it means for this clip. With several clips selected, **Loudness** reads "—". **Status** does too, unless the de-esser is off on the first of them, when it reads "off".
493	
494	**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−41.7 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.
495	
496	**Status** says where the de-esser acts, or why it isn't working:
497	
498	| Status | What it means |
499	| --- | --- |
500	| off | **Reduce sibilance** isn't ticked. |
501	| Acts above −41.7 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. |
502	| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. |
503	| Not de-essing: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
504	| Not de-essing: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
505	| Not de-essing: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |
506	
507	Until the clip's loudness is measured it plays without the de-esser, and an export waits. See [Before the clip's loudness is measured](/audio/gate/#before-the-clips-loudness-is-measured).
508	
509	## Good to know
510	
511	- The de-esser runs after the [gate](/audio/gate/) and the [leveller](/audio/leveller/), and before the [compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
512	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls write the action's end. The numbers glide across the action, and turning the de-esser on or off changes at the action's end.
513	- The de-esser does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
514

2:title: "Animate sound with actions"
3:description: Change a clip's sound over time with actions, from a pan sweep to an EQ that opens up, and what can't be animated.
9:An [action](/motion/actions/) can change a clip's sound as it plays: a pan sweeps across, an EQ band rises, the isolated voice fades in. What you hear in the preview is what an export writes.
12:  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
14:  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound, with an action selected"
15:  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end']}
22:1. Move the playhead to where the change should start, and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/) with <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>.
24:2. [Select the action](/motion/select-an-action/) and open the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
26:3. Set the controls to how they should be when the action ends.
32:## What an action can animate
34:With an action selected, these write that action's end state instead of the clip's own settings:
47:Numbers move smoothly across the action's span. Switches hold their start value and change at the action's end, with no glide, as at a cut between two clips.
58:Unticking a section or an EQ slot with an action selected turns it off at the action's end.
60:A number only glides while its section is on at both ends of the action. A section an action turns on arrives at its end values when the action ends. Voice Isolation's **Amount** and Noise Reduction's **Remove noise** are the exceptions. Each is one amount, and 0 is its off, so it glides up from 0 or down to it.
64:These always change the clip's own settings, even with an action selected:
72:A row like this shows ⊘ in front of its label while an action is selected. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
76:[Normalize](/audio/normalize/), [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) also write the clip's own settings with an action selected. The **Normalize** button carries a small boxed "clip" tag to show this.
78:## Processing turned on by an action
80:A clip gets whatever preparation its sound needs when an action asks for it, even if the clip's own setting is off:
82:- The isolated voice is made when an action raises **Amount**, on a clip whose own Voice Isolation is off.

8:`normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio` and `sync_audio` measure sound, so they share three things:
9-
10-- **They take no `scope`.** They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open. To work inside a nest, open it first. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
11-- **They can take seconds.** A clip with processing is rendered to be measured, which takes longer on a long clip.
12-- **They give up if the project changes meanwhile.** Nothing changes, and the answer says to call again.
13-
14-All four are one undo step, and a second identical call changes nothing.

18-Splits a clip's sound onto its own clip on the track below. It's **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (<kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>), see [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

157-
158-Gives clips the loudness and speech tone of a reference clip. It's **Clip ▸ Match Audio…**, see [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/), whose sheet picks the reference among the selected clips and has a **Loudness** and an **EQ** box.

161-| --- | --- | --- | --- |

163-| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change. At least one. |
164-| `loudness` | boolean | No | Match the loudness, through the volume and limiter. Default: true. |
165-| `eq` | boolean | No | Match the tone, through the EQ's shelves and bands. Default: true. |
166-| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

3:description: "Every Sound tab control through one agent tool: volume, fades, ducking, pan, EQ, dynamics, voice isolation and voice effects."
25:    "gate": {}
33:- `duck`, `compressor`, `limiter`, `eq` and each of its slots, `hum`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser` and `voice` are objects, and they merge key by key.
35:- An empty object turns `limiter`, `gate`, `leveller` or an EQ slot on at its defaults, so `{"limiter": {}}` adds the limiter.
85:| `channels` | string | `both` (the default), `left`, `right` or `swapped`. `left` and `right` play that channel of a stereo source from both sides, and `swapped` exchanges them. It's first in the clip's chain after isolation, and a mono source ignores it. |
108:### Noise reduction and voice isolation
112:| `noise_reduction` | 0 to 1 | Reduces noise in the clip's sound. |
113:| `isolation` | 0 to 1 | Isolates a voice with Apple's on-device model, which also reduces room echo. 0 is off, 0.8 is the app's default and 1 leaves silence between words. |
115:Isolation is rendered offline. The clip plays without it until the render lands, and an export waits for it. A clip not at ×1 plays without it.
117:See [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/).
143:### Hum removal
145:`hum` notches out mains hum and its harmonics, after the EQ.
147:| `hum` key | Range | Default |
153:See [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/).
155:### Gate
157:`gate` is a downward expander after noise reduction that turns the pauses down. Below the threshold the level drops by the ratio less 1 dB for each dB, and never by more than `range_db`.
159:| `gate` key | Range | Default |
168:The loudness it's relative to is what [`normalize_clip`](/mcp/tools-audio/#normalize_clip) reports, before the clip's volume. See [Gate](/audio/gate/).
172:`leveller` evens out a speaker who moves on and off the mic, after the gate. It's a gain curve made ahead of time from the clip's measured loudness and its speech, so it sounds the same in the preview and an export.
187:`de_esser` comes after the leveller. It turns the band above `frequency` down on sibilance and never boosts it.
189:| `de_esser` key | Range | Default |
195:The gate, leveller and de-esser act only once the clip's loudness is measured. Until then the clip plays without them, and an export waits. A clip too short or too quiet to measure plays without them, and on a nest clip they do nothing. See [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/).
199:`voice` replaces the clip's sound with a rendered effect, after isolation and before the channel pick.
222:Volume, mute, the fades, `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation` can all animate. `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` can't, and only `set_audio` sets them.

7:There is only one kind of track. Any track can hold a clip with sound, whether it is a video file, an audio-only file (a voice-over, music, a recorder's take) or a clip you split off with Detach Audio. A clip with sound shows its waveform in the timeline.
191:Ducking lowers every *other* clip while this one plays. The usual use is to turn on ducking for a voice-over clip so the music drops under it.
211:With **Speech**, the others go down only while this clip's speech plays: the attack starts Pre-roll before each stretch of speech, the level holds until Hold after it ends, and the release follows. Stretches close enough that their pre-roll and hold meet count as one, and a breath under 0.2 s between words doesn't lift the music.
227:Voice Isolation keeps the voice and removes what is around it: background noise, music, and the echo of the room. It uses Apple's on-device voice model, so nothing leaves your Mac.
--why

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct Hum {
    pub frequency: i64,
    pub depth_db: f64,
    pub harmonics: i64,
}

impl Default for Hum {
    /// 60 Hz mains, 30 dB deep, four harmonics.
    fn default() -> Self {
        Hum {
            frequency: 60,
            depth_db: 30.0,
            harmonics: 4,
        }
    }
}

/// Which channels of a stereo source play (spec §11 AU-34): `left` and
    pub threshold_db: f64,
    /// dB, 1…24.
    pub range_db: f64,
}

impl Default for DeEsser {
    /// 6 kHz, at the clip's loudness, 6 dB deep.
    fn default() -> Self {
        DeEsser {
            frequency: 6_000.0,
            threshold_db: 0.0,
            range_db: 6.0,
        }
    }
}

### Hum removal

`hum` notches out mains hum and its harmonics, after the EQ.

| `hum` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frequency` | 50 or 60 Hz | 60 |
| `depth_db` | 6 to 60 dB | 30 |
| `harmonics` | 1 to 8 | 4 |

### De-esser

`de_esser` comes after the leveller. It turns the band above `frequency` down on sibilance and never boosts it.

| `de_esser` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frequency` | 2,000 to 12,000 Hz | 6,000 |
| `threshold_db` | −30 to 20 dB, relative to the clip's loudness | 0 |
| `range_db` | 1 to 24 dB | 6 |

The patch follows the rules of [Patches](/mcp/patches/):

- A key you leave out keeps what's stored.
- `duck`, `compressor`, `limiter`, `eq` and each of its slots, `hum`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser` and `voice` are objects, and they merge key by key.
- `null` on one of those clears it, so `{"duck": null}` turns ducking off.
- An empty object turns `limiter`, `gate`, `leveller` or an EQ slot on at its defaults, so `{"limiter": {}}` adds the limiter.

**Answers** with the [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). A patch that changes nothing answers "made no change".

--shots

26:Each section header shows a one-line summary of its state, so you can read a clip's setup with every section closed. The summary is drawn a little stronger when the section differs from its default.
28:| Section | What it's for | Its summary reads | **Reset** does |
39:| [Gate](/audio/gate/) | Turns the pauses between phrases down | The threshold, such as "−10 dB", or "off" | Turns it off |
48:Click a header to open or close its section. Every section starts closed, and Frame Job remembers what you open and close. If the tab would show nothing but closed headers, the first section you haven't closed yourself opens.
52:Each header has a **Reset** button that appears when the section differs from its default. It's one undo step, and it reaches every selected clip.
15:  needs="Nothing. Speech detection and voice isolation run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
40:It reads the clip before any of the settings it's about to write: its loudness and true peak, and, every 10 ms of the part that plays, whether the clip is speaking or pausing. It needs at least a second of speech, and half a second of pause to measure the noise between words.
56:| Noisy | Turns on [voice isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) at 80 % with noise reduction off, and fits a [gate](/audio/gate/) to the pauses. |
57:| Noisy, on a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame | Turns on [noise reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) at 50 % with voice isolation off, because isolation can't serve that clip, and fits the gate. |
58:| Quiet | Turns voice isolation, noise reduction and the gate off. |
61:The gate opens 10 dB above the pauses' median true peak, held between −40 and −6 dB from the clip's loudness.
67:### De-esser
69:It turns on the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) at its defaults when at least 5 % of the speech has a hot "s" band: 6 kHz and up, within 10 dB of the clip's loudness. Otherwise it's turned off.
101:## Check its gate by ear
103:Enhance Voice sets the gate from the pauses it measured. On a voice with very soft word starts, the gate can bite into them, so listen to those words and lower the [gate](/audio/gate/)'s threshold if you need to.
109:- Measuring takes time in proportion to the clip's length, and it waits for the clip's voice isolation to render first.
120:- [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
